item.title: “Why laughter, why joy, When the world is always burning? Shrouded in darkness, Why do you not seek a light?” “Behold this painted image, This…
item.description:
“Why laughter, why joy,
When the world is always burning?
Shrouded in darkness,
Why do you not seek a light?”

“Behold this painted image,
This heap of wounds,
Diseased, full of many thoughts,
Of nothing stable or lasting.”

“This form is worn out,
A nest of diseases, fragile;
This putrid mass breaks apart —
Death is the end of life.”

“Like a gourd in autumn,
Abandoned and cast away,
Seeing these bleached bones,
What pleasure can there be?”

From: Dhammapada 146-156
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, abandon one thing. I guarantee you no further rebirth. What one thing? Greed, monks, is that one thing. Abandon it! I guarantee you no…
item.description:
“Monks, abandon one thing. I guarantee you no further rebirth. What one thing? Greed, monks, is that one thing. Abandon it! I guarantee you no further rebirth.” The Blessed One spoke this meaning. Here it is said:

With greed, beings,
Infatuated, go to a bad destination.
But the meditator, with right knowledge,
Abandons that greed.
Having abandoned it, he never
Returns to this world again.

From: Itivuttaka 1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: - What binds the world? By subduing what is one freed? By abandoning what thing Are all bonds destroyed? - Wish binds the world, By…
item.description:
- What binds the world?
By subduing what is one freed?
By abandoning what thing
Are all bonds destroyed?
- Wish binds the world,
By subduing sensual desire one is freed,
By abandoning wish,
All fetters are destroyed.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.69

item.title: “Monks, a man, attending to his own male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment — becomes lustful and…
item.description:
“Monks, a man, attending to his own male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment — becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, he attends to external female faculties, female deportment, female attire, female nature, female desires, female voice, female adornment, and becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, he desires external bonding. With that bonding as condition, pleasure and joy arise, and he desires that pleasure and joy. Monks, through delighting in their own masculinity, beings become bonded to women. Thus, monks, a man does not escape his own masculinity.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.51
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, knowing form as impermanent … knowing feeling as impermanent … knowing perception as impermanent … knowing formations as impermanent … knowing consciousness as impermanent,…
item.description:
“Monks, knowing form as impermanent … knowing feeling as impermanent … knowing perception as impermanent … knowing formations as impermanent … knowing consciousness as impermanent, changing, fading, ceasing — he sees all consciousness, past and present, as impermanent, suffering, subject to change. Seeing thus with correct wisdom as it actually is, all sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are abandoned. Being abandoned, he does not become distressed. Not being distressed, he dwells at ease. Dwelling at ease, that monk is called ‘one who has stilled all signs and is wholly inclined toward Nibbāna.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.43
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if a monk, while attending to some sign and giving attention to it, has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arise.…
item.description:
“Monks, if a monk, while attending to some sign and giving attention to it, has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arise. That monk attends to a different sign connected with what is wholesome, not that sign. Those evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion are abandoned and subside. With their abandonment, the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 20 – Vitakkasaṇṭhānasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Lakuṇṭaka-Bhaddiya: “Outside the parks, At the Ambāṭaka woodland, In the forest with its groves, Having abandoned craving, the root of craving, Bhaddiya sits in…
item.description:
Elder Lakuṇṭaka-Bhaddiya:

“Outside the parks,
At the Ambāṭaka woodland,
In the forest with its groves,
Having abandoned craving, the root of craving,
Bhaddiya sits in meditation —
Blissful, happy.”

Some people delight
In drums, flutes, and cymbals.
But I, at the root of a tree,
Delight in the Buddha’s teaching.

If the Buddha grants a gift,
I receive that gift.
I bear mindfulness of the body,
Constantly in all realms.

Those who mock me for my body,
Or follow me for my voice —
They do not know me,
Driven by sensual desire.

Not knowing the inside,
Not seeing the outside —
Blocked on all sides, the fool
Is carried away by words.

Not knowing the inside,
But seeing the outside —
Seeing only the external fruit,
He too is carried away by words.

Knowing the inside with wisdom,
Seeing the outside as well —
Seeing without obstruction,
He is not carried away by words.

From: Theragāthā 7.2
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights…
item.description:
“Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. And, monks, one who does not delight in the eye does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.19
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust…
item.description:
“Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of craving, monks, these ten things should be developed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.237
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these five mental shackles. What five? Here, monks, a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these five mental shackles. What five? Here, monks, a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual pleasures. Monks, for a monk who is not free from lust … craving for sensual pleasures, his mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving. If one’s mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving, that is the first mental shackle.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.206
📖 Read this sutta
